archetype: Archetype 4 (Swiss & High-Contrast) adapted for Threat Intelligence
vibe: Professional, Dense, Credible, Technical, High-Contrast, Restrained

typography.guidelines: Use JetBrains Mono for all IDs, IP addresses, CVE numbers, and code blocks. Headings must use tight tracking. Body text should prioritize legibility. No Inter font.

spacing_and_layout.philosophy: Dense Information Architecture for analysts. Maximize data visibility while maintaining scanability.
spacing_and_layout.grid_system: The Control Room Grid. Use tight gaps (gap-4 or gap-1px for borders) and rigid column structures. Elements should snap into place without loose space.
spacing_and_layout.container_padding: p-4 or p-6 for data cards. Hero can have generous padding (py-24).
spacing_and_layout.surface_strategy: Grid Borders (The Technical Look). Minimal to no border-radius (rounded-none or rounded-sm). Use 1px solid borders to define edges. NO shadows, NO blurry glowing gradients (except for the 3D radar blips).
spacing_and_layout.table_styling: High contrast rows with subtle hover states (hover:bg-white/5). Use tabular-nums for numerical data.

components.hero: Must contain a highly optimized react-three-fiber canvas showing a 3D radar/network particle globe. The data overlays (total entries, latest disclosure) should sit cleanly over or adjacent to the 3D element.
components.badges: Status badges must use the defined status colors. Solid background with 10-20% opacity and a 1px solid border matching the status color. Text color should be the pure status color.
components.cards: Flat surfaces with 1px border. No shadows. Use border-zinc-800.
components.buttons: Primary CTA: White background, black text. Secondary CTA: Transparent background, 1px white/20 border, white text.
components.filters: Compact inputs and selects. Use JetBrains Mono for filter values when appropriate.
components.exposure_checker: Textarea should feel like a terminal input or code editor (darker background, monospace font). Heuristic warnings should appear as high-contrast alert boxes below.

3d_graphics.usage: Use only in the hero section. Create a wireframe sphere or point cloud representing a supply chain network. Implement a rotating radar sweep effect that highlights specific nodes (threat blips) in red or amber as it passes over them.
3d_graphics.lighting: Use ambientLight (low intensity) and pointLights on the 'blips' to make them glow. Set canvas background to transparent to blend with the #09090b page background.

visual_enhancers.textures: Optional subtle noise overlay (opacity 2-5%) on the overall background to give it a matte, physical monitor feel.
visual_enhancers.motion: Very restrained. Micro-interactions on hover (border color change). Entrance animations should be quick and snappy (no slow, floaty fades).

image_urls.description: Abstract dark network connections. Use as a fallback background texture for the hero if the 3D canvas takes time to load or as a subtle texture in the Exposure Checker section.

icons.guidelines: Use sharp, unrounded icons where possible. Keep icon sizes consistent (e.g., size={16} for inline text, size={20} for buttons).

instructions_to_main_agent: Strictly follow the color palette. Do NOT introduce new colors (no teal, no purple). Use pure red/amber/emerald only for threat status indicators.
Implement the hero 3D visual using @react-three/fiber. It must be a rotating wireframe or particle sphere with 'radar blip' nodes that glow.
Ensure all text is accessible against the dark background. Use text-zinc-400 for secondary text to maintain hierarchy without losing legibility.
Do NOT use standard rounded cards. Apply rounded-none or rounded-sm to all Shadcn components (Cards, Buttons, Inputs).
For the Database page, ensure high information density. Use a table layout or a dense grid of border-collapsed cards.
Ensure the fonts (Chivo, IBM Plex Sans, JetBrains Mono) are imported correctly via Next/Google Fonts.
Add 'data-testid' to all interactive elements (buttons, inputs, filters, table rows) using kebab-case role-based names.
